title: Mecanum Kinematics

hints.title: The four kinematic equations
hints.content: The equations are: `fl = forward - strafe - rotation`, `fr = forward + strafe + rotation`, `bl = forward + strafe - rotation`, `br = forward - strafe + rotation`. With forward=0.6, strafe=0.4, rotation=0.3: fl=-0.1, fr=1.3, bl=0.7, br=0.5.

hints.title: Finding the maximum absolute value
hints.content: Use nested `Math.max()` calls: `double max = Math.max(Math.abs(fl), Math.max(Math.abs(fr), Math.max(Math.abs(bl), Math.abs(br))));`. This finds the largest magnitude among all four powers.

hints.title: How normalization works
hints.content: If `max > 1.0`, divide every power by `max`: `fl /= max; fr /= max; bl /= max; br /= max;`. Since max is 1.3, the front-right goes from 1.3 to 1.0, and all others scale proportionally. Do not normalize if max is already at or below 1.0.

hints.title: Putting it all together
hints.content: Four steps: (1) Compute raw powers with the kinematic equations. (2) Find the max absolute value. (3) If max > 1.0, divide all powers by max. (4) Call `setPower()` on each motor with the normalized value.
